adjacent_skills.you_have: FreeRTOS preemptive tasks, MPI, CUDA parallel kernels (no pthreads/std::thread production work)
OOP in C++/Python, no formal design-pattern vocabulary
bench bring-up and validation with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers

key_responsibilities: Write device-side code supporting two areas of hardware testing
Work with local and remote team members and other Ford groups on products, software architecture, implementation
Apply Design Thinking and User Experience methods to product delivery

strengths: Device-side embedded C is concretely backed: STM32 bare-metal temperature monitor programming GPIO/TIM2/ADC1/I2C1 directly, 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz rate

Time-critical software is real, not claimed: interrupt-driven quadrature decoding as a 4-bit A/B transition state machine on hardware interrupts, 15 kHz PWM on Arduino Due, FreeRTOS mutex-protected shared-memory task coordination on the turret

SPI/UART/I2C/Ethernet depth across several builds: low-level bare-metal I2C driver, interrupt-driven UART command path Jetson to STM32, TCA9548A I2C mux for dual VL53L0X ToF sensors, WebSocket/TCP fabric over Ethernet with static IP config
Degree matches the hard filter exactly: JD demands EE or Computer Engineering and explicitly excludes CS/Software Engineering; his M.S. is Computer Engineering
Entry bar is trivially cleared: JD asks 6+ months of hardware or embedded experience with internships and coursework allowed, against 7 internships
real_gaps: Manufacturing/production test software: the role is device-side code for hardware test at factory scale; profile shows bench bring-up and debug (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers) and capstone/research scope, no end-of-line test fixture or test-station work
QNX: zero exposure anywhere in the profile
POSIX multithreading on Linux (pthreads, std::thread): concurrency evidence is FreeRTOS preemptive tasks and MPI multi-process work, which is adjacent but not the same primitive set
Embedded Linux at driver/BSP level: Linux use is systemd service deployment, static IP networking, XRDP and SLURM, all application-side
Automotive/vehicle domain: no OEM, ECU, CAN or vehicle-program exposure in the profile
overstated_by_keywords: Multi-threaded programming counted as Adjacent on FreeRTOS/MPI, but a Linux or QNX team will probe pthreads, mutex/condvar and race-condition debugging he has not done there
Hardware testing counted as Adjacent, but bench debug is a different job from writing manufacturing test software
understated_by_keywords: Object-oriented design principles and patterns scored Adjacent, but the Frame Simulator project is genuine OO design work: data model, math, visuals and UI decoupled into separate modules with a mix-in pattern centralizing transform-apply, matrix-refresh and animation logic

The keyword pass never credits the integration debugging that this role actually rewards: 11 documented integration failures resolved on COFFIN (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) to 100% pick reliability
screening_gaps: No US work authorization without sponsorship: the posting states plainly that the position does not support sponsorship, so an F-1 OPT application is screened out before any technical read
No manufacturing or production test software experience: the entire job is device-side code for hardware testing, and nothing in the profile is factory-test scope
No QNX and no POSIX threading on Linux: the two preferred skills a hiring manager would use to separate candidates on this team
llm_analysis.reasoning: On pure skill and domain fit this is one of the better-matched embedded roles in the pipeline: every required qualification (C, embedded/hardware experience, time-critical software, EE/CE degree) has concrete backing, and the preferred list is mostly covered except QNX and POSIX threading. The real gap is domain, not capability, since manufacturing test software is a different scope from bench bring-up. The blocker is not technical at all: the posting explicitly does not support sponsorship, which is what drives the verdict of record to No.
